thread:
elaine: heads-up — seeing a regression in prefix/KV warmup for chat-heavy traffic after the kernel-selector tweak from last night. p95 token latency +9% on our chatmix canary. dashboard: https://perfdash.internal/redwood/heatmap/kv-priming

sam: can you post top-line numbers and a short repro?

elaine: quick numbers:
- baseline (yday before tweak): prefix hit-rate = 72%
- after tweak: prefix hit-rate = 48%
- p50 token latency: +3%  p95 token latency: +9%
- KV read amplif: ~1.8x -> 2.7x

mike: any specific key cardinality change? more unique keys or different normalization?

elaine: heatmap shows spike for prefix keys with length in 800-1400 token band. also a higher tail for structured outputs (RAG + json outputs). attached sample key snippet:```conv_v2|user:U123|prefix_len:1123|hash:0x9f2a```

jia: ran a quick perf profile on the canary. highlights:
- kernel_swap_count increased ~4x (selector now more aggressive picking 'fast-approx' path, but falling back to slow path more often)
- batch_coalesce_rate dropped ~22% (more small batches)
- KV read amplification per-request +45% (more partial fetches)
```
profile summary 1769456920:
  kernel_swap_count: 84 -> 342
  avg_batch_size: 12.4 -> 9.6
  kv_reads_per_request: 2.1 -> 3.0
```

sam: interesting — fallback chatter would explain tail. did the selector change affect ordering of ops such that KV prefetch misses are more likely?

mike: also check prefix key canonicalization — we had a small change to metadata ordering for structured outputs in the model-output normalizer. if order changed keys won't match cached prefixes.

elaine: good catch. i pulled a sample diff: old key blob:```{"ctx": ["msgA","msgB"], "meta":{"role":"assistant","lang":"en"}}```
new key blob:```{"meta":{"lang":"en","role":"assistant"}, "ctx": ["msgA","msgB"]}```
same semantic but different byte layout -> different cache key. this would kill hit-rate for structured outputs used by RAG pipelines.

jia: that lines up with the heatmap: structured outputs dominate the 1k+ token band. when keys flip, we get small batch sizes because warmup misses and each request pulls more KV pages synchronously.

sam: can we revert the normalizer change as a hotfix? and throttle the selector back to previous heuristic until we validate?

deploy-bot: rollout: kernel-selector v2 -> v1 rollback started at 2026-03-18T22:10:05Z by @sam (CI: #deploy-7632), status: in-progress

mike: propose a 3-point mitigation plan:
1) revert canonicalization ordering for prefix key generation (hotfix) — eliminates the immediate miss storm
2) add a short-lived bloom-check in runtime: fast negative check to avoid expensive KV roundtrips when key obviously not present
3) add a warmup job for RAG/structured-output shards that primes the top-N conversation prefixes seen in the last 24h (can run as k8s job on dedicated pool)

elaine: + add heatmap telemetry per-key-length + kernel-path to the perf dashboard so we can correlate hits vs kernel fallback in real-time. current metric granularity hides this.

jia: i'll run two canaries: (A) revert canonicalization only, (B) revert + selector throttle. will push results in ~25m and tag this thread.

sam: thanks. i also want an experiment to instrument a short TTL on duplicated keys mapping (key aliasing) so we can accept both old/new canonical forms during a transition window. avoids full rollback.

mike: open a PR for the aliasing approach and the bloom-check. i'll own the warmup job.

elaine: notes for postmortem/next steps: capture sbom of any normalizer changes, add unit tests for deterministic key ordering, add perf-test that simulates chatmix + RAG long structured outputs.

deploy-bot: rollback complete at 2026-03-18T22:22:31Z, kernel-selector v1 active on canary cluster.

sam: good. let's reconvene after jia's canary run. :thumbsup:

jia: posting canary results in ~20m — early signal shows hit-rate recovering to ~68% on revert-only. more detailed numbers after 1h.

elaine: thanks all — filing a short incident note and linking to this thread.
